facts.claim: A task-run failure event must carry `sandbox_backend` in every emitter: the per-run status activity (`update_task_run_status._capture_terminal_analytics`), the workflow-level `task_run_failed` metrics/log event in both `process_task/workflow.py` (`ProcessTaskWorkflow.run` exception handler) and the duplicated `execute_sandbox/workflow.py` (`ExecuteSandboxWorkflow.run`), the agent-reported PATCH path (`facade/api.py:update_task_run`), and the direct model helper (`models.py:TaskRun.mark_failed`). These are five independent emission points for the same logical event (`task_run_failed`/terminal analytics) that must be kept in sync whenever a new attribution field is added, because the activity-based emitter is skipped on an already-terminal transition (the PATCH/mark_failed paths own the capture in that case) — so the field has to be added to all paths, not just the 'canonical' one.
facts.evidence: "This activity performs the DB status transition, so it is the single canonical emitter of the terminal analytics events for workflow-driven runs" (update_task_run_status.py:_capture_terminal_analytics docstring) combined with "This PATCH performed the DB transition, so it owns the task_run_failed capture. The workflow's status-update activity sees the row already FAILED and skips its own capture" (facade/api.py comment) — i.e. three+ mutually-exclusive emitters for the same event.

facts.claim: `TaskProcessingContext.sandbox_backend` (set once per run by `_resolve_sandbox_backend` in `get_task_processing_context.py`) is NOT automatically preserved across a Temporal `continue_as_new` hand-off — the continuation re-fetches `TaskProcessingContext` via `_get_task_processing_context`, which would re-resolve the backend from scratch and could disagree with the backend the sandbox was actually created on. To keep it stable, the chosen backend must be threaded explicitly through `ResumedSandboxState` (added field `sandbox_backend`), written in `_build_resumed_input`, and re-applied onto `self._context.sandbox_backend` in `ProcessTaskWorkflow.run` right after `_get_task_processing_context` returns, when `input.resumed_sandbox is not None`.
facts.evidence: workflow.py: `self._context = await self._get_task_processing_context(input)` followed by `if input.resumed_sandbox is not None and input.resumed_sandbox.sandbox_backend is not None: self._context.sandbox_backend = input.resumed_sandbox.sandbox_backend`; also `TaskRun.prepare_for_cloud_resume` explicitly does `state.pop("sandbox_backend", None)` with the comment "the resumed run re-resolves its backend from scratch, so a stale `hogland` must not survive..." — confirming the backend is not naturally sticky across resumes/continuations.

facts.claim: `execute_sandbox/workflow.py` (`ExecuteSandboxWorkflow`) is a deliberate near-duplicate of `process_task/workflow.py` (`ProcessTaskWorkflow`), created to allow a traffic cutover without patching the original Temporal workflow; it is slated for deletion in a later PR. Any change to `process_task`'s failure/event-emission logic (progress emission, `task_run_failed` properties, `_update_task_run_status`) likely needs the mirrored change in `execute_sandbox/workflow.py` until that deletion happens.
